blog.title: It Wasn’t the Fertiliser — the Roots Never Took Hold of the Soil

blocks.x: You are already a new creation — so why aren’t you yet living out the new life?
A fruit tree fertilised to death

When I was young I saw something in the countryside. An old gardener was transplanting a fruit tree. Because he was in a hurry, he simply stood the tree in the hole, threw a loose layer of soil over it, and rushed off to water it and fertilise it. For the next three months he watered it every day and fertilised it every day. After three months, the tree was dead.
The old gardener said something I have remembered all my life: “It wasn’t the fertiliser. The roots never took hold of the soil.”

I often think of a sister. She had been a believer for fifteen years, never missed a meeting, and had filled seven notebooks with Bible-reading notes — yet she was still the mother who came home and screamed at her children. Through her tears she asked: I’ve read the Bible for all these years — what on earth is wrong with me?
Brothers and sisters, could it be that the problem isn’t the fertiliser, but the roots?
What changes a life is not method but position
The Bible says: “Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new” (2 Corinthians 5:17).
Notice Paul’s words. He didn’t say, “If anyone works very hard,” nor, “If anyone has the right method.” What he said was — “If anyone is in Christ.”

“In Christ” is a position, not a degree. A person cannot be “a little bit in Christ,” any more than a baby can be “a little bit born.” Many believers today don’t lack methods; they lack position. We have Bible-reading plans, prayer charts and a calendar packed with ministry — all of it fertiliser — yet we seldom stop to ask: have this tree’s roots taken hold of the soil?

So what is “in Christ”? The Lord himself gave the answer: “If you remain in me, and my words remain in you” (John 15:7). “Remain” in the original means taking up residence, not visiting. So to be in Christ is to live in his word — not only knowing it, but obeying it.
What you feed is what grows
This brings us back to “See, Listen, Think, Speak, Do.”

What you see shapes your thinking; what you hear shapes your beliefs. If what we see is the world and what we hear is the flesh, our thinking, speaking and doing will all drift away from God; if what we see is Christ and what we hear is God’s word, our thinking, speaking and doing will be renewed. So the starting point of transformation is not “Do” but “See” and “Listen.”
It’s like a polluted river. If you only stand downstream fishing out rubbish, but won’t walk upstream and shut off the waste pipe, you can fish all your life and the river will still be dirty.

In his famous Bobo doll experiment of 1961, the psychologist Bandura found that children who had merely seen an adult behave violently would afterwards imitate the very same behaviour on their own. A great deal of human behaviour is learned not from lectures but from observation. What you look at, you slowly become.

Seeing and listening are Information; thinking and speaking are Revelation and Conviction; doing is Implementation. Repeated practice becomes habit, habit becomes character, and character becomes life. Research from University College London indicates that a new habit takes on average about sixty-six days to become automatic — so a habit isn’t formed on the day you feel like it; it is formed on the days when you feel nothing and do it anyway.
Remember the parable? Feed the white dog, starve the black dog. What you feed is what grows; what you choose is what you become.

You are already a new creation — God accomplished that for you once and for all, and it cannot be shaken. But whether you live out the new life depends on your choices every day. When you keep remaining in Christ, letting his word come into you and living it out, the old things will pass away naturally, and the new life will be truly revealed.
It isn’t that you drove the old things out; it’s that the new life grew, and the old was left with no room.
You are not only a new creation — you will live out a whole new life.
Questions for reflection

Over the past seven days, what was the ratio between the time you spent on screens and the time you spent in God’s word? This week, which entrance of “seeing” or “listening” will you close, and which will you open?

Author: Paul, writing from Macedonia around AD 55–56, during his third missionary journey.

Quote 2 Corinthians 5:14–15: the love of Christ constrains us, so that we no longer live to ourselves.
Point out the order: first the love of Christ, then no longer living to ourselves, and only then a new creation.
321 connection: the old self is self-centred; the new self is selfless.

Background: the night the Lord was betrayed — his farewell words on the way to Gethsemane (John 13–17).

In Christ = living in his word; also quote John 15:10: keep my commandments and you will remain in my love.
Quote James 1:22: be doers of the word, and not only hearers.

321 connection: this is exactly the eight stages of changing our mindset — Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation, Evaluation, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication.

brief12.title: 5. Choose the Right Cultivation
notes: Seeing and listening are in themselves neutral
The key is what you let in
Feed the white dog, starve the black dog
What you feed is what grows
Key points:
The eye is not sin, the ear is not sin; a field is neutral — whatever you sow is what grows.
Retell the story of the white dog and the black dog: which one wins? The one you feed.
We don’t overcome by beating the old self to death, but by cutting off one food supply and switching to another; quote Galatians 2:20.
Quote Galatians 6:7: whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.
321 application: the 920 practice — everyone I relate to is my “2”; live out selflessness and bear the ninefold fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22–23).

brief12.title: Practices
notes: Adjust the source: what I see and hear
Practise the life of being in Christ
Build a cycle of life renewal
Go deeper with the eight stages of changing our mindset
Key points:
Practice one: record three days of screen time and Bible time; set one subtraction and one addition.
Practice two: pick just one verse each day and find one opportunity to actually obey it that day.
Practice three: design a daily cycle — see and listen in the early morning, think during the day, speak in the evening, do at any moment.
Go deeper with the eight stages: Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation, Evaluation, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication.
Reminder: keep it up for at least sixty-six days, and find a “2” partner to give each other an account.

brief12.title: Closing and Call
notes: You are already a new creation
Whether you live out the new life
depends on your choices every day
Let Jesus be King over your seeing, listening, thinking, speaking and doing
Key points:
Return to the old gardener’s words: it wasn’t the fertiliser; the roots never took hold of the soil.
Restate the lesson’s conclusion: the old things will pass away naturally, and the new life will be truly revealed.
Key addition: it isn’t that we drive the old things out; the new life grows, and the old is left with no room.

The 321 Two Core Values: let Jesus be King; let Jesus receive all the glory.

brief12.title: Prayer of Response and Blessing
notes: Lord, I am willing to remain in you
and to let your words remain in me

brief21.title: Living Out New Life in Christ
notes: Why Seeing, Listening, Thinking, Speaking and Doing Matter (Part 2)
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.
The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.”
(2 Corinthians 5:17)
Key points:
Greet warmly; explain that this is Morning Devotion 321 Lesson 118, Part 2 of “Why Seeing, Listening, Thinking, Speaking and Doing Matter”.
Read the full theme verse, 2 Corinthians 5:17, and invite the brothers and sisters to read it aloud together once.
Preview the lesson’s five steps: foundation, process, breakthrough, process of transformation, choice.
Set the tone in one sentence: what changes a life is not method but position.

brief21.title: Introduction (1): An Honest Question
notes: The growth of life lies in cultivation
The key to cultivation: See, Listen, Think, Speak, Do
So why do some people follow the steps
yet their lives still don’t break through?
Key points:
Review the last lesson: the growth of life lies in cultivation; the key to cultivation is See, Listen, Think, Speak, Do.

brief21.title: Introduction (2): Not the Fertiliser, but the Roots
notes: The old gardener watered and fertilised every day
After three months, the fruit tree still died
“It wasn’t the fertiliser.
The roots never took hold of the soil.”

brief21.title: Theme Verse and Background
notes: Paul writes from Macedonia around AD 55
to the church in prosperous, corrupt Corinth
The love of Christ constrains us — no longer living to ourselves
(2 Corinthians 5:14–17)
Key points:
Author: Paul, writing from Macedonia around AD 55–56, during his third missionary journey.
Corinth: capital of Achaia, a two-port commercial city on an isthmus, with Cenchreae to the east and Lechaeum to the west.
The believers’ old life was just around the corner, their old friends next door, their old habits knocking at the door every day.

brief21.title: 1. The Foundation of Life: In Christ
notes: What changes a life is not method
but position
In Christ → a new creation
Outside Christ → the old life

Stress where the emphasis falls: Paul doesn’t say “if anyone works very hard”; he says “if anyone is in Christ”.

brief21.title: “In Christ” Is a Position, Not a Degree
notes: Greek: ἐν Χριστῷ
Paul’s most frequent coordinate
No one is “a little bit in Christ”
just as no baby is “a little bit born”
Key points:
Greek ἐν Χριστῷ (en Christō), together with its equivalents, is one of the most frequent expressions in Paul’s letters.
The difference between a word of position and a word of degree: either you are in, or you are out.

brief21.title: In Christ = Living in His Word
notes: “If you remain in me,
and my words remain in you”
(John 15:7)
Not only knowing, but obeying
Key points:
Background: the night the Lord was betrayed — his farewell words on the way to Gethsemane (John 13–17).
“Remain” Greek μένω (menō): taking up residence, not visiting; it occurs more than ten times in John 15:1–11.
Quote John 15:10: if you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love; the Lord himself first kept his Father’s commandments.
Quote James 1:22: be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
You may quote Dallas Willard: “Grace is not opposed to effort, it is opposed to earning.”

brief21.title: 2. The Process of Life: From New Creation to Renewal
notes: Misunderstanding: completely changed the moment you believe

being made new (process)
“From glory to glory” (2 Corinthians 3:18)
Key points:
Clear up the misunderstanding: three months after believing, people find the old faults still there and doubt whether they were ever saved.
“New creation” καινὴ κτίσις; “new” is καινός — new in nature, not new in time.
Standing God gives once for all; the process grows every day; quote 2 Corinthians 3:18 and Ephesians 4:22–24.
Picture: a newborn is fully a human being from birth, yet must learn to walk and talk.
The 321 fivefold change: mindset, life, daily living, relationships, ministry.

brief21.title: The Key in Between: Let the Old Things Pass Away
notes: The old doesn’t vanish because you hate it

that it gradually loses its power
Not only a new identity, but a new way of living
Key points:
Paul doesn’t say the old things vanish automatically, but that they have passed away — already dealt with on the cross.
Face it honestly: some old things we can’t bear to let go of; we take them out and polish them every day.
Scientific support: a saying generally attributed to Carla Shatz summarising Hebb’s theory (1949) — “Neurons that fire together wire together.”
Quote Ephesians 2:10: we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works.
Picture: a released prisoner who still lives next to the prison and keeps a prisoner’s routine — his status has changed, but his life has not.

brief21.title: 3. Breakthrough Begins with “See” and “Listen”
notes: What you see shapes your thinking
What you hear shapes your beliefs
“Keep your heart with all diligence,
for out of it is the wellspring of life” (Proverbs 4:23)
Key points:
We often want to change the outcome, but won’t touch the source; “Think” comes from “See” and “Listen”.
Read the full verse of Proverbs 4:23: out of it is the wellspring of life.
The Lord on the two entrances: Matthew 6:22 the eye is the lamp of the body; Mark 4:24 take heed what you hear.
Scientific fact: the optic nerve of a single eye carries more than a million nerve fibres sending signals into the brain.
The eye is not a passive camera; it is an intake.

brief21.title: Two Paths, Two Kinds of Life
notes: See the world, hear the flesh:
thinking, speaking and doing drift from God
See Christ, hear God’s word:
thinking, speaking and doing are renewed
Key points:
Quote Romans 12:2: don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.
“Conformed” carries the sense of being pressed into the same mould as this age; the world doesn’t use force, it uses a mould.
Psychological support: Bandura’s 1961 Bobo doll experiment and Social Learning Theory (1977) — people learn by observation.
Picture: a polluted river — if you only fish out rubbish downstream and never shut the waste pipe upstream, it stays dirty all your life.
321: the focus is Jesus — not ourselves, not other people, not our circumstances.

brief21.title: One Hand Closes, One Hand Opens
notes: “I will set no vile thing before my eyes”
(Psalm 101:3)
“Think about these things”
(Philippians 4:8)
Key points:
David’s vow (Psalm 101:3) closes a door; Paul’s list (Philippians 4:8) opens one.
Spiritual growth always needs both hands: one closing, one opening.
Make it concrete: the last fifteen minutes before sleep and the first thing on waking — that is upstream.
Affirm the congregation: sitting here this morning for morning devotion is itself an upstream decision.
The 321 order of relationships: first with God, then with ourselves, then with others, last of all with things.

brief21.title: 4. The Process of Life Transformation
notes: See, Listen → Information
Think, Speak → Revelation and Conviction
Do → Implementation
Repeated practice → habit
Key points:
Reminder: information is not the same as revelation; many people have plenty of information but very little revelation.
The depth of “Think”: Joshua 1:8 “meditate on it day and night”, Hebrew הָגָה — chewing over and over, like a cow chewing the cud.
“Speak” confirms conviction: Matthew 12:34, out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
Encourage sharing in small groups, retelling at home, bearing witness at work — pressing revelation into life.
The 321 eight stages: Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation, Evaluation, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication.

brief21.title: From Habit to Life
notes: Habit → character
Character → life
A new habit takes about sixty-six days on average
This is how a new creation lives out new life
Key points:
Data: Lally et al., 2010, European Journal of Social Psychology — about sixty-six days on average, with wide individual differences.
Key line: habits are formed on the days when you feel nothing and do it anyway.
Research by Wood et al. (2002) indicates that a large share of daily behaviour is automatically repeated habit.
The saying generally attributed to Frank Outlaw: thoughts become words, words become actions, actions become habits, habits become character.
Point out that Scripture said it earlier and more deeply: the source is in seeing and hearing, and the destination is not destiny but the life of Christ.

brief21.title: 5. Choose the Right Cultivation
notes: Seeing and listening are in themselves neutral
The key is what you let in
Wrong seeing and hearing → a wrong life
Right seeing and hearing → a right life
Key points:
The eye is not sin, the ear is not sin; God made the eye to behold his glory.
Picture: a field is neutral — sow wheat and you get wheat, sow tares and you get tares; sow nothing and you get weeds.
Quote John 15:5: apart from me you can do nothing.
Ask: over the past seven days, what was the ratio of screen time to time in God’s word?

brief21.title: Feed the White Dog, Starve the Black Dog
notes: What you feed is what grows
What you choose is what you become
“Whatever a man sows,
that he will also reap” (Galatians 6:7)
Key points:
Retell the story of the white dog and the black dog: which one wins? The one you feed.
Key: we don’t overcome by beating the old self to death, but by cutting off one food supply and switching to another; quote Galatians 2:20.

321: the old self is self-centred, the new self is selfless; selflessness is not having nothing, but Christ living in me.
The 920 practice: everyone I relate to is my “2”; bear the ninefold fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22–23).

brief21.title: Practices (1)

Less worldly input
More of God’s word

Make See, Listen, Think, Speak, Do a daily habit
