brief12.title: Seeing Rightly
notes: When the Eyes Are Opened, Life Is Turned Around
“Open my eyes,
that I may see wondrous things out of your law.”
Key points:
Greet warmly, addressing “brothers and sisters”; explain that this is Lesson 119, “Seeing Rightly (1)”.
Read the full theme verse, Psalm 119:18, once, and let the Scripture speak for itself.
Point out what is special about this prayer: it doesn’t ask for a change of circumstances, only “open my eyes”.
Preview the whole lesson in one sentence: when the eyes are opened, life is turned around.

brief12.title: Introduction: The Problem Isn’t Out There
notes: Hubble pointed at an empty patch of night sky
Ten days’ exposure revealed three thousand galaxies
The sky didn’t change; the seeing did
Not a new sky, but new eyes
Key points:
Tell the story of the Hubble Deep Field, December 1995: aimed at a tiny empty patch of sky, exposed for ten days, revealing some three thousand galaxies.
Key line: that night the sky didn’t change; what changed was the ability to see.
Quote Proust, In Search of Lost Time: the real voyage of discovery consists not in seeking new landscapes, but in having new eyes.
Bring out the theme: we haven’t come to trade in our sky, but to ask the Lord for new eyes.
Link to the 321 fivefold change: change the mindset, and the life changes.

brief12.title: Theme Verse and Background
notes: Psalm 119: the longest chapter in the Bible
In trouble, he asks the Lord to open his eyes
Paul prays for believers from prison in Rome
Asking God to enlighten the eyes of the heart (Ephesians 1:18)
Key points:
Psalm 119 is the longest chapter in the whole Bible, 176 verses, an acrostic poem in 22 stanzas.
The writer was in trouble — derided, persecuted, weary with sorrow — yet asked not for different circumstances, only for opened eyes.
“Open” (gālāh) means “to lift off a covering”; “wondrous things” is the word often used for miracles like the Red Sea.
Paul wrote Ephesians from prison in Rome around AD 60, praying for believers in a city of idols.
You may mention Calvin’s image in the Institutes of the Christian Religion: Scripture is a pair of spectacles God gives us.

brief12.title: 1. Two Kinds of Eyes: Worldly Eyes
notes: “Their eyes were opened”
(Genesis 3:7)
Looking at self, at shame, at lack
Result: fear, hiding, covering up
Key points:
Stress that these weren’t physical eyes being opened — Adam could already see, and had even named the animals.
Compare the serpent’s promise in Genesis 3:5: “your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”
Genesis 3:10: “I was afraid… so I hid myself.” Three steps: fear, distance, covering up.
The fig-leaf covering = today’s degrees, job titles, performance figures and retouched photos.
321: worldly eyes are self-centred eyes; pride is leaving our originally intended position and wanting to take God’s place.

brief12.title: 1. Two Kinds of Eyes: Spiritual Eyes
notes: “Having the eyes of your hearts enlightened”
(Ephesians 1:18)
Seeing God’s glory, promises and heart
Eyes opened, they recognised Jesus (Luke 24:31)
Key points:
“Enlightened” Greek phōtizō — the subject is God; we cannot open them by our own effort.
321: the Holy Spirit is my guide; rely on the heart and the Holy Spirit, not on the brain and ourselves.
The disciples on the road to Emmaus: Luke 24:16 “their eyes were kept from recognizing him”.
At the breaking of bread their eyes were opened — when spiritual eyes open, people recognise Jesus.
321: the focus is Jesus — not ourselves, not other people, not our circumstances.

brief12.title: 2. Wrong Seeing: It Leads People Away from God
notes: “When the woman saw that the tree…” (Genesis 3:6)
Looking at appearance: a delight to the eyes
Looking at gain: good for food
Looking at self: to be desired to make one wise
Key points:
The fall began with the word “saw”; the tree had always been there — what went wrong was this particular act of seeing.
Our eyes are shaped by the words we listen to — listen to the serpent, and you see the world through the serpent’s eyes.
Lot lifted his eyes and saw the plain of the Jordan (Genesis 13:10); Abram lifted his because God told him to (Genesis 13:14–15).
Science: the human eye has a physiological blind spot, and the brain fills it in automatically, so we think we see completely.
Psychology: Peter Wason’s “confirmation bias” (1960) — we first believe, and then see.

brief12.title: 3. Right Seeing: It Brings People Back to God
notes: Open my eyes (Psalm 119:18)
Seeing God, the truth, heavenly reality
Eyes opened, from darkness to light
from the power of Satan to God (Acts 26:18)
Key points:
Right seeing is grace, not technique — it takes the form of a prayer.
2 Kings 6:17: Elisha asked the Lord to open his servant’s eyes, and he saw the mountain full of chariots and horses of fire.
Science: visible light spans only about 380 to 750 nanometres, a minute fraction of the electromagnetic spectrum.
2 Corinthians 4:18: “the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.”
The 321 shift in perspective: from man’s to God’s, from the earthly to the heavenly, from the temporary to the eternal.

brief12.title: 4. Once the Eyes Are Opened, the Life Is Turned Around
notes: “Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes”
(Acts 9:18)
Outwardly, sight restored
In essence, spiritual eyes opened
Key points:
Saul knew Scripture thoroughly yet couldn’t see Jesus — those best at reading Scripture can be the blindest.
Acts 9:8: he opened his eyes and could not see; for three days he neither ate nor drank.
God first shut down his worldly eyes, then opened his spiritual ones.
Philippians 3:8: “I count all things to be a loss… and count them nothing but refuse.” The things didn’t change; the eyes that valued them did.
Psychology: Aaron T. Beck’s cognitive therapy (1960s) — what determines our emotions is interpretation, not the event.

brief12.title: 5. As You See, So You Live
notes: Look at self → inferiority, shame, fear
Look at circumstances → anxiety, unease, pressure
Look at others → comparison, envy, hurt
Look at Jesus → peace; look at God → victory
Key points:
Matthew 6:22: “The lamp of the body is the eye.” The lamp decides whether the whole house is light or dark.
Peter sank not because the wind grew stronger, but because he “saw” that the wind was strong (Matthew 14:30).
Numbers 13:33: “We were in our own sight as grasshoppers.” How we place ourselves shapes how we feel about others.
Psychology: Simons and Chabris (1999, Perception), the gorilla experiment — almost half never saw it.
Application: we’re busy counting our own passes, and God’s works pass right in front of us unseen.

brief12.title: Practices for Daily Life
notes: Discern where your way of seeing comes from
Deliberately shift your focus
Pray every day for your eyes to be opened
Not your circumstances, but how you see
Key points:
Practice one: emotions are an alarm — anxiety usually means looking at circumstances, envy at other people, shame at yourself.
Practice two: the key word is “deliberately”; prepare three turning verses (Hebrews 12:2, 2 Corinthians 4:18, Psalm 121:1–2).
Practice three: pray Psalm 119:18 every day.
Go deeper with the eight stages: Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation, Evaluation, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication.
The 920 practice: look at every “2” around you with spiritual eyes.

brief12.title: Closing and Call
notes: When the eyes are wrong, life goes off course
When the eyes are right, life lights up
Seeing Jesus, fixing our eyes on Jesus
living out Jesus, entering victory
Key points:
Return to the opening sky: the galaxies were there all along, the chariots of fire were there all along, the Lord was there all along.
John 9:25: “though I was blind, now I see.”
Call: take off the glasses you’ve worn for so long and hand them to the Lord.
The 321 Two Core Values: let Jesus be King; let Jesus receive all the glory.
Close with the key line: seeing Jesus, fixing our eyes on Jesus, living out Jesus.

brief12.title: Prayer of Response and Blessing
notes: Lord, open my eyes!
Let me see everything through your eyes
Let Jesus be King in my life
May all the glory go to the Lord Jesus
Key points:
Lead the congregation in the declaration line by line, speaking slowly.

Pray for family members who don’t yet believe: “Lord, open the eyes of his heart.”
