2. The 321 insight: it is not events that change you; it is how you think that decides whether you overcome.
3. The first link in the fivefold change is mindset: change your mindset and your life changes.
4. One sentence to state the theme: today we receive four keys.

brief21.title: Key Verses and Background
notes: Slide text:
God’s word → hearing → thinking → faith → victory
Romans written around AD 56
“This is the victory that has overcome
the world: your faith.” 1 John 5:4
Key points:
1. Background to Romans: around AD 56–57, written by Paul in Corinth to the church in Rome.
2. Context: Israel did not lack zeal, but it was “not according to knowledge”, seeking to establish their own righteousness (Romans 10:2–3).
3. The chain: the word of Christ → hearing → faith → calling on him → salvation (Romans 10:13–17).
4. The original: “faith” is pistis, “hearing” is akoē — the message heard determines the weight of faith.
5. 1 John, written around AD 85–95 in Ephesus; “has overcome the world” is a completed tense — the victory is already accomplished.

brief21.title: 1. Right Thinking Is God-Centred
notes: Slide text:
Not optimism, but God-centredness.
Optimism says: I believe I can.
Faith says: I believe God can.
The focus is Jesus, not circumstances.
Key points:
1. Clear up the misunderstanding: right thinking is not the same as positive thinking or self-motivation.
2. Contrast: optimism focuses on myself; right thinking focuses on God.
3. Optimism is held up by emotion, and when the emotion collapses, everything collapses; right thinking stands on God’s word.
4. 321: the focus is Jesus — not ourselves, not other people, not our circumstances.

brief21.title: Return to 321
notes: Slide text:
Jesus is my role model, the Bible is my standard,
the Holy Spirit is my guide.
Let Jesus be King;
let Jesus receive all the glory.
Key points:
1. Read out in full the Three Foundations, the Two Core Values and the Goal.
2. The inner coordinates shift: from “What am I going to do?” to “What would Jesus do? What does the Bible say?”
3. Stress the Holy Spirit’s guidance: rely on the heart and the Holy Spirit, not on the brain and ourselves.
4. The Goal: establish God’s system.

brief21.title: Truth Is Always Greater Than the Facts
notes: Slide text:
Circumstances say: impossible, too late.
God says: possible, not too late.
“Just say the word,
and my servant will be healed.” Matthew 8:8
Key points:
1. Definitions: the facts are the situation your eyes can see; truth is God’s never-changing word.
2. Facts are temporary and earthly; truth is eternal and heavenly.
3. The centurion: a Roman officer’s chain-of-command reasoning — he looked at the authority of the word (Matthew 8:8–10).
4. Add: the centurion was a Gentile in an unfavourable position, yet he did not let the facts have the final word.

brief21.title: Thinking Determines Experience
notes: Slide text:
“She said within herself, ‘If I just touch
his garment, I will be made well.’” Matthew 9:21
Healing began with her thinking.
Beck: the power of automatic thoughts.
Key points:
1. The woman with the bleeding: Scripture deliberately says “she said within herself” — healing began with her thinking (Matthew 9:21).
2. Supporting evidence from psychology: Aaron T. Beck’s automatic thoughts, developed at the University of Pennsylvania in the 1960s.
3. Albert Ellis’s ABC model: what determines the Consequence (C) is not the Activating event (A) but the Belief (B).
4. The difference: psychology sees that “B” exists; the Bible tells us what “B” ought to contain — Colossians 3:2.

brief21.title: 2. Don’t Dwell on the Enemy’s Words
notes: Slide text:
Eve’s fall began with a thought.
Listen wrongly → look wrongly → think wrongly → act wrongly
Change the thinking and the action changes;
change the action and the ending changes.
Key points:
1. Genesis 3:1–6: the serpent spoke first; Eve then looked, then thought, and only then acted.
2. The route map: listen wrongly → look wrongly → think wrongly → act wrongly.
3. Stress: Eve’s fall began not with an action but with a thought.
4. 321: when the self-centred “self” is stirred up, the lie has a foothold.

brief21.title: Cut Off the Wrong Source
notes: Slide text:
Satan cannot compel anyone to sin;
his only skill is to “speak”.
A drop of ink in clear water —
the water is already different.
Key points:
1. The key: Satan has no power to compel anyone to sin; his only weapon is to “speak” (John 8:44).
2. Illustration: drop a drop of ink into clear water, and the water is already different.
3. Supporting evidence from psychology: Peter Wason identified confirmation bias in 1960 — once a lie moves in, the mind finds reasons for it.
4. Susan Nolen-Hoeksema’s research on rumination: going over it a few more times only digs the rut deeper.

brief21.title: It Is Written
notes: Slide text:
Tempted, the Lord did not debate;
three times he said: “It is written.”
Don’t debate with Satan;
the mind is not a toy but a battlefield.
Key points:
1. The Lord Jesus’ example: three temptations, three times “It is written” (Matthew 4:4).
2. The order in James 4:7: first submit to God, then resist the devil.
3. Martin Luther is commonly said to have put it: you cannot stop the birds flying over, but you can stop them building a nest.
4. Conclusion: don’t debate with Satan, don’t let the lie in; the mind is not a toy but a battlefield.

brief21.title: 3. Don’t Be Limited by the Past
notes: Slide text:
“Don’t remember the former things…
I will do a new thing.” Isaiah 43:18–19
Failed once, hurt once —
so sure that nothing will change this time.
Key points:
1. Background: just before this, Isaiah 43 recalls the way through the Red Sea, then says, “Don’t remember the former things.”
2. God is not asking people to forget his works, but not to lock him into the way he acted “that one time before”.
3. The two sentences of a heart bound by the past: this time nothing will change; God probably won’t act.
4. Reminder: experience is always smaller than God.

brief21.title: Faith with a Line Drawn by Experience
notes: Slide text:
“Lord, if you would have been here, my brother
wouldn’t have died.” John 11:21
They believed he could heal — they had seen it;
not that he could raise the dead.
Key points:
1. Martha and Mary said the same sentence, “If you would have been here” (John 11:21, 32).
2. They believed he could heal the sick, because they had seen it; they did not believe he could raise the dead, because they had never seen it.
3. Supporting evidence from psychology: Seligman and Maier’s learned helplessness experiments at the University of Pennsylvania in 1967.
4. Reminder: the door is actually open, yet the person no longer walks out.

brief21.title: Believe, and You Will See
notes: Slide text:
“If you believed, you would see
God’s glory.” (John 11:40)
Naaman washed seven times; the Lord touched —
different methods, the same God.
Key points:
1. Jesus’ order: not “see, then believe”, but “believe, and you will see” (John 11:40).
2. 2 Corinthians 5:7: “For we walk by faith, not by sight.”
3. Three ways of healing leprosy: Naaman washing seven times, the Lord’s touch, ten men cleansed on the road.
4. Neuroplasticity: Donald Hebb’s 1949 principle — repeated thinking wears in a new road.
5. Abraham’s example: he took account of his body as good as dead, yet was not weakened in faith (Romans 4:19–20).

brief21.title: 4. The Thinking of Faith Brings Victory
notes: Slide text:
“This is the victory that has overcome
the world: your faith.” 1 John 5:4
Where does faith come from? From our thinking.
Think on God’s word, and faith is built up.
Key points:
1. Key verse: 1 John 5:4 — the key to victory is faith.
2. The lifeline: God’s word → hearing → thinking → faith → victory.
3. Think on God’s word: faith is built up, life is lifted, circumstances are turned around.
4. Think on the negative: faith is weakened, emotions are crushed, life is trapped.

brief21.title: The Steering Wheel and the Grasshoppers
notes: Slide text:
Thinking is the wheel, life is the car.
Ten spies said: like grasshoppers.
Caleb said: we are well able to overcome!
Faith is not a feeling; it is a choice.
Key points:
1. Illustration: thinking is the steering wheel; set the direction wrong and the harder you try, the further off you go.
2. The contrast among the twelve spies: grasshopper thinking versus Caleb’s “well able to overcome” (Numbers 13:30, 33).
3. Defining faith: the “assurance” and “proof” of Hebrews 11:1 are the language of property, not of emotion.
4. Viktor Frankl: the freedom to choose one’s attitude in any set of circumstances cannot be taken away.
5. The eight thresholds of Philippians 4:8 — filter every thought before it comes in.

brief21.title: Practices 1 and 2
notes: Slide text:
When problems come, go back to God’s word
First ask: what does God’s word say?
Deliberately reject negative and lying thoughts;
replace them at once with God’s word.
Key points:
1. Practice 1: don’t start by analysing the circumstances; first ask what God’s word says.
2. The first four of the eight stages: Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation.
3. Practice 2: the moment a negative thought appears, replace it with a declaration of God’s word.
4. Evaluation and Correction: not suppression but replacement; an empty house will be occupied again.

brief21.title: Practice 3
notes: Slide text:
Practise thinking with faith every day;
think on and declare a promise again and again.
“I have hidden your word in my heart,
that I might not sin against you.” Psalm 119:11
Key points:
1. Practice 3: choose one promise — one verse, one week, morning, noon and night.
2. Repetition: spiritual pathways, like neural pathways, are worn in by repetition.
3. Multiplication: share what you have experienced with your “2”, and help someone begin to think rightly.
4. Scripture: Psalm 119:11.

brief21.title: Summing Up the 3-2-1 Vision
notes: Slide text:
The old self is self-centred; the new self is selfless;
humility overcomes pride, selflessness overcomes Satan.
Mindset → life → living → relationships → ministry
Life first, then relationships, then ministry.
Key points:
1. Sum up how the Three Foundations, Two Core Values and the Goal take shape in our thinking.
2. The old self is self-centred, the new self is selfless: almost all negative thoughts revolve around a “self”.
3. Humility is laying down our rights and returning to our originally intended position — let man be man and let God be God.
4. The fivefold change and its order: life first, then relationships, then ministry.
5. The 920 practice and 235 relationships: find a spiritual companion to think the truth through together.

brief21.title: Closing and Call

Think wrongly and you fall into trouble;

notes: Slide text:

Key points:
1. Lead the congregation in the lesson’s declarations of faith.
2. A short response prayer: ask the Holy Spirit to renew our hearts and minds every day.
