brief12.title: Right Speaking and Wrong Speaking
notes: Let my mouth be God’s outlet
I spoke not from myself
What I should say, and what I should speak
John 12:49
Key points:
1. Greet the congregation and name the theme: what is right speaking? What is wrong speaking?
2. Read the full key verse, John 12:49.
3. Stress the contrast: Jesus did not speak whenever he felt like it; he spoke only when the Father wanted him to.
4. Bring out the 321 thread: the self-centred life decides for itself what to say; selflessness lets God decide.

brief12.title: Four Hundred Million Words in a Lifetime
notes: About 16,000 words a day on average
Over 400 million words in a lifetime
Death and life are in the power of the tongue
Proverbs 18:21
Key points:
1. Data: Mehl et al., published in Science in 2007, tracked 396 university students; men and women alike averaged about 16,000 words a day.
2. Do the sum: live to seventy and you speak over 400 million words in a lifetime.
3. Illustration: “If I’d known, I’d never have married you” remembered for twenty years; “God still has a better plan” walking with someone for thirty years.
4. Read Proverbs 18:21 to bring out the weight of “speaking”.
5. Name the problem: we don’t lack the desire to say the right thing; we don’t know what counts as right or when to speak.

brief12.title: Key Passage and Background
notes: John written around AD 85–95
Chapter 12 ends the public ministry
The Word made flesh does not speak from himself
The Father sets the content and the manner
Key points:
1. Author: the apostle John; place of writing traditionally Ephesus; purpose: see John 20:31.
2. Context: John 12:36b — Jesus departed and hid himself; verses 44–50 are the last proclamation of his public ministry.
3. Culture: the Graeco-Roman world idolised eloquence; orators and sophists gained status by their words.
4. Tension: John 1:1 says “the Word was God”, yet this Word says, “I spoke not from myself.”
5. Application: if even the Word does not speak from himself, what right do we have to?

brief12.title: Not from Himself, Only from the Father
notes: The things which I speak, even as the Father has said to me, so I speak
John 12:50
The Son can do nothing of himself (John 5:19)
Speak by emotion, feeling, habit — and we get it wrong
Key points:
1. Original language: “say” is legō, stressing content; “speak” is laleō, stressing manner. The Father sets both content and manner.
2. Scripture interprets Scripture: John 5:19, 8:28, 14:10 — three times “not of myself”.
3. Illustration: at a car accident the first words were not “Are you hurt?” but “Can’t you drive?”
4. 321: pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility inspires humility, and both sides win.
5. Scripture: Proverbs 15:1 — a gentle answer turns away wrath.

brief12.title: Swift to Hear, Slow to Speak
notes: Swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger
James 1:19
Pause first, listen first, then speak
If Jesus were me, how would he say it?
Key points:
1. Original language: swift is tachys, slow is bradys; not silence, but a change of speed.
2. Psychology: Goleman’s “amygdala hijack”, from Emotional Intelligence (1995).
3. Research: Lieberman’s team, Psychological Science (2007) — naming emotions lowers amygdala activity.
4. Scripture: Psalm 141:3, asking the Lord to keep the door of our lips; 1 Samuel 3:10, “Speak; for your servant hears.”
5. 321: rely on the heart and the Holy Spirit and you rejoice; rely on the brain and yourself and you worry.

brief12.title: Speak More of What God Says to You
notes: We can’t help telling the things which we saw and heard
Acts 4:20
When it is inside, it comes out naturally
Let God’s word fill my mouth
Key points:

2. Original language: a double negative, “we are not able not to speak” — pressure from within, not bravado.
3. Compare Jeremiah 20:9: a burning fire shut up in my bones.
4. Reminder: when God moves you and shines his light on you, don’t just keep it in your heart — speak it out.
5. 321: the Bible is my standard; on the bookshelf it can’t govern the tongue, only in the mouth can it hold it in check.

brief12.title: Three Fruits of Speaking It Out
notes: Speak it out — it deepens

Speak it out — you live it out
In and out is living water; in only is a Dead Sea
Key points:
1. Research: MacLeod et al. (2010), the “production effect” — reading aloud is remembered better than reading silently.
2. Research: Ebbinghaus’s forgetting curve (1885).
3. Scripture: Romans 10:10, confessing with the mouth; Deuteronomy 6:6–7, talking of them when sitting, walking, lying down, rising up.
4. Illustration: the Sea of Galilee has an inflow and an outflow, so it lives; the Dead Sea has no outlet and its salt is about 30 per cent, so it is dead.

2. Original language: eucharisteō is made of “good” plus “grace” — literally, speaking well because of grace.

3. Order: first prayer and praise, then the great earthquake; first the fruit of lips, then the prison doors flung open.
4. Outcome: the jailer’s whole household saved (16:31), and the church in Philippi was born.
5. Contrast: Israel talked themselves out of the Promised Land; Paul talked the prison into a delivery room for the church.

brief21.title: The Focus Is Jesus, Not Our Circumstances
