Morning Devotion 321 · Lesson 143
• Greet: brothers and sisters, good morning; today is the third message on “doing rightly”.
• State the thread of the lesson: live out an example, bring victory, leave a legacy.
• There are six theme passages; the core is John 13:14–15.
• Keep the tone warm, and invite everyone to quieten their hearts and prepare to receive.
Introduction · Someone Is Watching How You Live
A new believer follows you for a week
What kind of Jesus will they learn?
Our lives are more honest than our mouths
Influence flows from daily living
• Ask: if someone spent a whole week with you, what kind of Jesus would they learn?
• Quote the mother: what I fear most is that my children will live exactly the way I do.
• Bandura’s 1961 Bobo doll experiment: people learn by watching and imitating.
• Jesus founded no seminary; he simply chose twelve men to be with him.
Background · The Lord Picked Up the Towel
The night before Passover: who is greatest?
The Lord rose and washed twelve pairs of feet
“I have given you an example”
• John 13 is the turning point of the book: from the book of signs to the book of glory.
• In the first century people walked dirt roads in sandals; foot-washing was the lowliest job in the household.
• Luke 22:24: the disciples were arguing about who was greatest.
• The greatest One in all the world stood up and picked up the towel.
Key Point 1 · Not Just Speaking, but Doing
He taught humility — and bent to wash feet
He taught love for enemies — and prayed on the cross
“Blessed are you if you do them”
• “Example” is hypodeigma in the original: a model script set out underneath for people to trace.
• The love for enemies taught on the mountain was carried out on the cross (Luke 23:34).
• Matthew 7: those who hear and do build on the rock; those who hear and don’t do build on the sand.
• Illustration: learning to swim from three books, then fished out ten seconds after getting in the water.
Key Point 1 · Jesus Is My Role Model
Not only learning what Jesus said
but learning how Jesus lived
A true disciple isn’t good at hearing sermons
but does what they say
• The first of the 321 Three Foundations: Jesus is my role model.
• Rizzolatti’s team discovered mirror neurons: seeing someone else do something, the brain responds as if doing it itself.
• A saying commonly attributed to Schweitzer: example is the only way to influence others.
• Philippians 2: he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant.
Key Point 2 · Doing Right Brings Victory
“Be subject therefore to God.
Resist the devil”
(James 4:7)
Victory is not fighting but obeying

• Wegner’s white bear experiment, 1987: the more we suppress a thought, the harder it rebounds.

Self-centred → wants control → defeat
Selfless → willing to obey → victory
Humility overcomes pride
No longer I, but Christ
• The root of Satan’s fall was pride: the five “I will”s of Isaiah 14.

• Selflessness is not having nothing, but entering into the infinite (Galatians 2:20).
• Bonhoeffer: only those who believe obey, and only those who obey believe.
Key Point 3 · Doing Right Brings Influence
“Be imitators of me”
(1 Corinthians 11:1)
Life isn’t passed on by talking
Life first, then relationships, then ministry

• 2 Timothy 2:2: Paul, Timothy, faithful men, others — four generations.

• 321 practice: 920, living out selflessness; 235, building spiritual family and team.

Feet into the water — then the water is cut off
“As they went, they were cleansed”
Go and do it, and you will experience God

• Joshua 3: in flood season, only when the feet entered the water did the river rise up in a heap.
• Jacobson’s 1996 study of behavioural activation: action comes first, and motivation catches up.
• Psalm 18:32: it is God who makes my way perfect, not I myself.

Live out one aspect of Jesus each day
When wronged, choose a different response
Do one thing for someone else each day
Ask the Lord for strength before you act
• Don’t try to do too much; one thing at a time. Lally’s research: habits take on average sixty-six days to become automatic.

• 1 John 3:18: not in word only, but in deed and truth.
• Develop an awareness that you are an example: someone is watching me, someone is learning from me.

Not merely a change of behaviour
but the revealing of a life
Personal victory, community revival
Let Jesus be King in you

• Three calls: over our pride, our wounds and our footsteps, let Jesus be King.
• Begin to live out Jesus and you become a message; keep living him out and you become an example.
